div.p: CC e e Ce

Skelhorne came out of his shell. He was as lively as a cricket. • Oldham did net like his tricks. So they sent three men. to mark him. But the three were of very little use. Skelhorne simply ran away from them. He will do still greater things. • Clare was not so speedy as usual. His spurts lacked the characteristic dash. Why was it, " Number twelve"? Perhaps it was due to the greasy ground. Perhaps it was owing to lack of chances.

div.head: ci c
div.p: ci c

Ruddick delights in mud-larking. He was the muddiest man on the field. The outside coating he got through The amount of hard work he did. If Ruddick was often at Watersheddings, Oldham would have to returf the ground. His side steps ploughed up the grass. When Anlezark tried to follow him. .Anlezark usually sat in the mud. The Oldham "wizard" was out-tricked. Ruddick scored over him every time. Anlezark .was a man of wrath.

div.head: COOC c c
div.p: COOC c c

Waywell did particularly well. V. Farnsworth didn't like. his tackling. Renwick 'showed a turn of speed. He twice \had hard lines in not scoring. What was' the matter, Jolley? - You were not quite up to form. There were a few bad slips made. You were a marked man from the start. That's the worst of possessing a reputation. The Oldham threequarters' orders were Before the match started; "Keep an eye on .Jolley." Perhaps that accounted for all that happened.

The second team did well, didn't.they? It was a fine win over Oldham "A." • DainOth was the •life of his side. • The Oldham cracks were puzzled with him. • A. Bramhall had an attack of the "nerves." He did net de himself justice at all. More experience will change all that. A. Brown is a master hand at the game. He well *deserved the cheers he got. His was the best try of the match. Perhaps the best of the " A.'s " this season. The others all played a ding-dong game.

div.head: ROMANCE OF A HUSPITAL.
div.p: ROMANCE OF A HUSPITAL.
Miss Ethel Burrows, an Irish nurse, hag left Belfast for South Africa to be married to Mr. Herbert Walton, a wealthy real estate proprietor ..at Ladysniith, Orange River Colony.

The meetineof Miss Burrow; and her fiancO was of a romantic character. Miss Burrows was a probationer in a nursing home in Belfast. The day following the last "Twelfth of July" Mr. Walton, who was on a visit to Ireland, met with an accident, fracturing his skull bad sustaining other injuries. He was brought to the Royal Victoria Hospital, and as all the regular hos- pital nurses were at the time fully engaged otherwise, Miss Burrows \ was brought in to Attend him. Three weeks later Mr. Walton re- covered consciousness, and eventually became convalescent. A warm friendship between nurse and patient developed into riper affection, and before leav- ing for South Africa he had obtained the girl's promise to become his wife. Her mother's death intervening prevented her accompanying him out.

A verdict of "Accidental death" was returned at an inquest at Kearsley on the body of Mr. Herbert Hardy (44), under-manager at the Clifton and Kearsley Coal Company's No. 1 New- t6wn Colliery, who was killed by a fall of roof in the mine.
John Topping (56), joiner, of an, who fell while repairing some spouting behind a house at Platt Bridge owing to his ladder slipping, has succumbed tos. his injuries at the Wigan Infir- mary.

div.head: First Division.
div.p: First Division.
Orfcrd Barracks v. Crosfield's.

This match was played on the Barracks ground. Teams: Orford Barracks: Moody-; Busby and Lomax; Callon, Staples and Stevens; Campbell, Birkenhead, Forshaw, Roberts and Trafford. Crosfield's : Gleave; Johnson and. Sherratt; Cartey, Wells and Wright; Kimber- ley, Rawlinson, Bellfield,: Ray and Wilkinson. Crosfield's won the toss and Forshaw set the ball rolling, before a fair number of spectators. The home players quickly got possession, and the ball was sent out to Roberts, who raced along the touch and shot when near the., corner flag. He scored a magnificent goal in the first minute. Encouraged with this early success, the home players made tracts for the visitors' goal, when Forshaw scored a second goal. The visitors could not overcome the home defence and were penned up in their own half. TraEord and Forshaw twice .added further goals. Up to this point the visitors .had not crossed the centre line. Then their forwards began to. work to- gather in better style, and their half-backs had better control of the home forwards. From a piece of grand combination play,Bellfield scored a lovely goal for the visitors. At half-time the Soldiers led by five goals to one. The second half commenced with Cros-Eeld's having the best of the exchanges, but gradually the Soldiers began to assert their superiority, when the visitors' half-back line failed to holi the home forwards. Tlik visitors' backs kicked very erratically, which gave the home forwards plenty of chances, and Trafford (two) and, For- shaw (two) added further goals. making the total nine goals against one in favour of the Barracks.

' Gleave, in the visitors' goal, was very good, in suite of the score recorded against him, and he was unfortunate in colliding against the up- right while making a grand save, but he stuck to his work very bravely. Crosfield's were Poorly served by. their hacks, their play leaving much to be desired. The Soldiers played very well all round, Campbell dribbling and centre- ing finely. • Several gods were scored from his good work. Trafford and Forshaw were quick at snanning lin the chances which came their way 7 and scored three and five goals respectively.

div.head: Fairfield United v. Emmanuel.
div.p: Fairfield United v. Emmanuel.

Played at Orford-road. Teams: Fairfield United: Gibbs Rowlands and Woodhouse; Rigby, Hamblett and Dooley; Collins, Gleave, Betibington, Simcock and Oxley. Emmanuel: Knight; Harrison and Harding; Lawless, Hatton and O'Brien; Wainwright, Caldwell, Potter, Isherwood and Green. The home team started the game with ten men, and the opening stages were in favour of the visitors, but owing to poor shooting Gibbs was not seriously troubled. Fol- lowing a good passing movement, Caldwell failed when in an easy position. The home centre now put in an appearance, and imme- diately the game turned in favour of the homo- sters, Bebbington leading a strong attack on the visitors' goal, and, fastening on a centre from the left, he opened the score, Knight fail- ing to hold the ball. The home goal was now besieged by the visitors. and Rowlands. by good.- defensive play, drove them back. Bebbingon, by a splendid piece of individual play, succeeded in scoring a second goal. The 'Fairfield half- backs were now feeding their forwards very well, and a grand shot from the right hit the cross- , bar, and Oxley, following up, scored from the rebound. Half-time: Fairfield, three goals; Emmanuel, nil. On resuming, Emmanuel made several changes in the positions of their players, which proved to be effective. O'Brien played well in the centre and the home defence had a very warm time of it.. At this period the visitors had tlui misfortune to , lose the services of Harrison, , through a sprained ankle, hut still had the best of the play. O'Brien beat Gibbs with a good drive. Following this reverse, Knight was severely tested, but Bebbington managed ,to beat him again and completed the "hat trick." These reverses only served to make the visitors play up more strongly, and Green scored their second ' goal. Right up to the close the home goal was severely taxed, but their defence held out, and the final score was: Fairfield United, four , goals; Emmanuel, two goals.

div.head: WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT LEAGUE.
div.p: WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT LEAGUE.
Second Division.

Defeat of the Prospective Champions. On the Excelsior's ground, Bewsey-lan.e. Players :—Excelsior: Jackson; Morris and Wareham; O'Neil, Spencer and Hunt; Walker, Leah, Pritchard, Holmes and Hughes-Cox. Orford St John's: Forver ; Smith and Millward ; U. Smith, Denny and Atherton; Matthews, Tickle, Stretford, 3.leachin and Hankinson. The game started at a red-hot pace, and St. John's was the first to attack, but they met with a resolute defence, Jackson keeping goal very well under heavy pressure. End-to-end play . ensued ,for a time, .when the home vanguard made a 'raid on St. John's goal, and Walker scored with a fine shot. Encouraged by this success, the home team" continued to press, and Walker again scored for the Excelsior. Fol- lowing this second reverse, St. John's woke up and played determinedly, and the home defence faltering under heavy siege, Millwarcl, the visitors' back, scored for his side. At this juncture Atherton was hurt and had to leave the field. The visitors, now left with ten men, were able to hold their own, and half-time was called: Excelsior, two goals; St.. John's, ono goal. On resuming, Atherton returned; and both teams played keen. Every incli was eor,leqed, but Walker proved to he a thorn in St john's defence. Forver, mulling the ball, allowed it to roll over the line, and thus the home team were three up. There appeared to be no nold• • ing the Excelsior just now, and St. John's Ile- fence had a troublesome time. A brilliant ' effort by Leah ended in that player registering a fourth goal. St. John's did not. relish these reverses, and the appearance of their first., defeat made them play more strenuously. They pressed home their attack, Hankiftson doing the needful. The Visitors kept up the pace, and Tickle snapped up an opening and scored ' the kllird goal for St. John's. Seeing that there was a chance of yet retrieving their position, the St. John's played for all they were worth, but the home defence was not to be beaten again, and time was called with the Excelsior being the first to iiifiict defeat on St.,John's this season.

div.head: FRIENDLY MATCHES.
div.p: FRIENDLY MATCHES.
Padgate United v. Adult School.

On the Pad gate ground. Players :—Padgate: Norke; Warburton and Hankinson; Rigby, Wadsworth and Williams; James Houghton, Darbyshire, J. Houghton, J. Rigby. and S. fla.rd- man. Adult School : Dykes; Garnett and ' Spencer; Leigh, Hunter and Clarke; Rhodes, Jackson, Rowe,- Webb and Banner. Referee, Mr. C.- S. Esseithigh. The home forwards made an advance on the visitors' goal, but the backs cleared smartly. Banner received the ball, ran along the touch-line, and shot at goal. Norke was deceived by the flight of the ball and the first goal was scored for the visitors. Rhodes was instrumental in scoring the second and third goals, while Webb added a fourth. The visitors lead at half-time by four goals to nil. From the restart play was very even during the first twenty minutes. Then Webb scored . again, and soon after Rowe added the sixth. Wadsworth scored for the home team from a free-kick for "hands." The visitors ran out: easy winners by six goals to one.

div.head: Stockfion Heath Defeat Lymm Amateurs in the Replayed Cup-tie.
div.p: Stockfion Heath Defeat Lymm Amateurs in the Replayed Cup-tie.
THE CHAMPIONS DEFEAT LATCHFORD.

The most important and interesting fixture amongst the North Cheshire League Clubs on Saturday was the meeting of Latchford and Lostock Gralam, on the Thelwall-lane enclosure. As neither club had lost a match in the competi- tion this was the tit-bit of the day's programme. A very keen and interesting contest was, wit- nessed. The first half was very even, both sides scoring a goal each, and it was in the secOnd portion when the struggle came for the winning point. Both defencea were severely taxed, but they got through their work very well. A few minutes before time Parker registered the win- ning goal. The home forwards did not appear to make the best of their chances, as on many occasions during the second portion of the game they allowed the visitors' backs to have clear kicks at the ball,when a little more dash on their part would have been the possible means of Pulling the match off as a win. Had the game ended in.a draw it would have.been a fair criterion of the play.

The Crosfield -Recreation Club received the Altrincham Lads' team at Folly-lane, when, owing to stile heavy rain, the ground was in a bad condition, and good combinatien was at a discount. The game was fairly even and keenly fought, with the visitors slightly the better, deserving their lead of one goal to nil at half- time. On turning round, the home players made a great improvement in their football, and after several .attacks on the visitors' goal, during which time Berry was the shining light, Balm- forth gave a foul in the penalty area, and Forster took the kick and equalised. Soon after Crosfield's obtained the lead, Munn scoring from a well-placed corner.

Ough-trington -United Reserves entertained St. Margaret's Reserves at Heatley, *here the game was very even during the first half, the home team leading by two goals to one. On resuming, the homesters added four other goals, while the visitors replied once. Both teams Were awarded penalty kicks,- from which they scored. The visitors played a far better game than the score seems to indicate.
Stockton Heath Win.

The match of most importance to the enthu- siast of Stockton Heath was the replayed cup-tie between the village team and Lymm Amateurs, which was played on the Amateurs' ground. Both teams had several changes from the first meeting, and it was With no certainty that the " Heathens " made the journey, as, after play- ing, ,a drawn game, the advantage lay with the team on its ,own ground. From the kick-off the " Heathens " played up with much determina- tion, and it was soon evident they were not going to leave anything to chance, as they went very quickly round the home goal. At the end of five minutes' play Jones scored with a .beautiful shot, a lead they retained up to,the interval. On the resumption both teams played hard for points, and the home team werks suc- cessful in equalising about midway through the second portion. Then came the battle for supremacy. The visitors were unfortunate in having a goal disallowed, the whistle blowing as the ball passed between the posts. Not dis- mayed, they held on to their game; and ten minutes from the finish Jones again scored and put his side in front.
By 4 4 Linesman."

Postells and Cross; Walker, Howard, Weedall, Costello and Smith. The home team set the ball rolling. The first run was made by the visitors' right wing, Bardsley heading away, and, from a free-kick, Smith, on the home right, made a grand centre,- which Parkes cleared. The visitors were pulled up for offside against Weedall. The home middle line set their forwards going, and Taylor sent in a grand shot, causing Garnett to handle. A .warm attack on the visitors' quarters ended in the ball being sent over the line. Parkes inter- cepted a tine pass by Fogg. The ball *as taken to the opposite end, where Robinson miskicked with a clear field, but recovered the ball and placed it out of danger. Taylor made a fine shot at goal and forced Garnett to concede a corner, which was got away. A good return by Bardsley saw Reeves mull the ball, and Lees dashed in and Scored for the home side.

The visitors now pressed strongly, and Kite. made two good saves. From a long shot by Parkes a grand opening was spoiled by offside, and 'Smith, for the visitors, placed the sphere over the bar with a shot from the line. Cross, at half-back, was looking well after the home right wing, and little progress could be made. Weedall was foiled by Bardsley, who sent the ball well up the field, and Reeves gave a corner away when he had plenty of time to clear. A good combined run by the visitors saw Weedall hit the crossbar, and Costello, from the rebound, gained a corner, which proved fruitless. The visitors were having as much play now as their opponents, Denton doing some effective work at half-back. Downs had to concede a corner, and from the ensuing flag-kick Kite showed up very well, saying shots in fine style. At this period the Gralamites were pressing hard and gained several corners. Robinson and Bardsley were fine in defence. End-to-end play followed. The ball travelled very quickly, and Haspell and then Smith caused Garnett to clear hurriedly. Costello, by a' fine movement, transferred play to the other end, but met .a sound defence. Ha.s- pell was' again unlucky, a fine shot hitting the upright, when the goalkeeper was at .the other end. From the goal-kick Postells passed the ball to Costello, and he to Weedall, when well placed, and the latter made no mistake. He scored a fine goal and made the scores equal. From the centre-kick the visitors were approach- ing the home goal, when an accident to Costello caused a brief stoppage. Half-time arrived with the score one goal each. After change of ends the visitors were the first to become aggressive. BardSley cleared his lines at .the second attempt, the ball going into. touch in the visitors' half. Owing to the greasy state of the ground miskicks were very frequent and play somewhat suffered by long kicking being indulged in by both sets of players. Reeves was next prominent by good, judicious play when hard pressed by the home forwards, and a fine centre by Smith went across the goal- mouth, with nobody there to intercept it. A fine chance was lost. From the -goal-kick the visitors had the best of the exchanges, and a foul against Postells brought relief. Reeves and Parlvte cleared with big kicks, and a Corner to the vitl,ors did not benefit them. The Gra- lamites were now keeping the home team in their own half, and it was only good work by Webb, Bardsley and Robinson, that kept their goal from *falling. Kite had to save a good shot from Weedall, and Downs transferred play, only for Taylor to get offside. The visiting forwards joined in a grand run from the centre of the field, when Robinson nipped in at the opportune time and cleared what appeared to be a certain goal. Fogg and Taylor now changed places, and a little im- provement was seen on the left, and for a short time the visitors' defence was kept busy, but they kept their charge intact. A raid into the home half saw Robinson give a foul just outside the penalty area, and Parkes scored for the visitors, the ball glancing into the net off one of the home side. The home team made several attempts to get equal, but too much loose passing spoilt their work. The visitors' backs were allowed to have clear kicks all the time, and on time being called they ran out winners by two goals to one.
Crosfield's Recreation v. Altrincham Lads.

Played at Folly-lane before a poor attendance of supporters. Teams :—Crosiield's: Moores; Shaw and Clemo; Bretherton, Worrall and Scott; Sherratt, Forster, Munn, Whitfield and HawthOrne. Altrincham Lads: Berry; Shaw and Balmforth; Dunn, Walker and Greetly; Bowland, Stephens, Barnet, Crews and Owen. Referee, Mr. S. Breeze. The ball travelled quickly from end to end and neither side could claim much advantage during the early portions of the game, until the visitors got down to the home quarters and were successful in register- ing the first point. They managed to retain their lead until the interval.

On resuming, the home players were quickly on the aggressive, and tested the visitors' defence, Berry saving splendidly on , several occasions. Worrall was continually breaking up the combination of the visitors. In an at- tack upon the visitors' citadel a penalty was given against Balmforth. Forster, taking the kick, steered the ball into the net and equalised the scores.

From the centre the game was carried to the visitors' goal area and Berry was early called upon. At time the players came under the referee's restriction for rough play. The home team were having the best of the game and a corner was conceded, the ball being finely placed in the mouth of the goal. Munn directed the sphere into the net and put the homesters in front. From the centre-kick the visitors gradually got down and made several attempts to get through, but the home defence was on the alert and staved off the, attack. Result: Crosfield's Recreation, two; Altrincham, one.

, . The visitors have to thank their goalkeeper for his exhibition between the uprights, as he was chiefly the means of saving his side from a heavy defeat. Worrall` was the pick of the home defenders, and Forster. Hawthorne and Whitfield were smart in the forward line.

div.head: WARRINGTON LEAGUE NOTES.
div.p: WARRINGTON LEAGUE NOTES.

Orford Barracks and Crosfiekl's Recreation Reserves were in opposition, on the ground' of the former, when the game proved to be very much bne-sided. The Soldiers showed much superior form throughout, and through fine play by Campbell, Forshaw and Trafford they put the ball past Gleave, the visitors' custodian, nine times, while Crosfield's were only able to reply once through Bellfierd. The most exciting and interesting match in the competition was the meeting of the Excel- sior and Orford St. John's, at - Bewsey-road, where a very hard and fast game was witnessed. The home team set about their work with deter- mination, while the visitors appeared to be too confident of their abilities, and for the. first 15 minutes treated their opponents .rather Only after -Walker had scored two goals did they seem to realise that they were in arrears. From the centre-kick St. John's Made a strong attack on the home citadel, but were met with a sound defence, and then Millward managed to score with a good shot. The visitors goal- keeper did not make very good clearances, owing to the greasy condition of the ball. Leah scored a fourth for the home team. The visitors played very hard to avert defeat, and Rankin- son and Tickle scored for St. John's. The home defence played a grand game. St. John's failed to score again and they had to retire defeated by four goals to three. This was their first defeat this season.

The meeting of Fairfield United and Emmanuel proved a very interesting match, in which the home team surprised their most ardent supporters by winning their first match of the season: The home team started with ten players, and were able to hold their own, but when Bebbington arrived he soon made his pre- sence felt by quickly scoring two goals. During the second portion the visitors lost the services of Harrison and were defeated by four goals against two goals. -

div.head: NORTH CHESHIRE LEAGUE. Firit Division.
div.p: NORTH CHESHIRE LEAGUE. Firit Division.
Latchford v. Lostock Gralam.

This match was played at Thelwall-lane, before a fair croivd of spectators. Unfortunately for the home club's exchequer, it began to rain shortly after noon, and this had its effect on the attendance. The verdict went to the visitors, but from the general run of the game a draw would have been a true reflex of the game. The teams were :—Latchford: Kite; Robinson and Bardsley ; Downs, Webb and Carter; Smith, Haspell, Lees, Fogg and Taylor. Lostock Gralam : Garnett; Parkes and Reeves; Denton,

div.head: CHESHIRE AMATEUR CUP. Replayed Tie. Lymm Amateurs v. Stockton Heath.
div.p: CHESHIRE AMATEUR CUP. Replayed Tie. Lymm Amateurs v. Stockton Heath.

This replayed cup-tie took place on the Amateurs' ground. The "Heathens" won the toss and the home centre set the ball rolling, and Marsh, obtaining possession, sent out to Jackson, who, racing down the left, made a fine centre and put the home goal in danger. A timely kick by Hudson transferred the leather to midfield. Give-and-take was the form of play for a while, when Denny, by -a well-judged pass, set Jackson going, and he made a fine dribble, down the field, and, passing the ball to Jones, in the centre, the latter drove the ball past Saville. He scored for the visitors after five minutes Play. From the centre-kick the game was keenly contested, the sides being very evenly matched. The defence on both sides was good, and the kicking and the tackling were splendid. Jones, the visitors' centre, , made a grand individual attempt on the home ' goal, only to see his final shot cannon of a defending back out of play for a corner. Magill placed the ball so well in front of goal that Saville had to exert all his abilities as a goal- keeper to clear his lines. Nothing further of note took place up to the interval, when .the "Heathens" were leading by one goal to nil. -On resuming, the opening passages were quiet, the visitors being the first to assume the aggres- sive. A timely clearance ,by Millington only prevented the visitors from scoring. Even play, in midfield followed for a short period, and Gos- ling, in checking an attack, was laid out, but resumed after a brief stoppage. The " Heathens " at this time were rather unfor- tunate,.as by a good piece of play by their for- wards Smith shot the ball past Saville. The point wits disallowed for a foul on the former player. The visitors were now doing most of the pressing. Antrobus centred finely from the right, and Jackson headed just wide of the post. From the goal-kick the home team took up the running, and paid a visit to the "Heathens'",

end. Owing to slack defensive play, Harrison gave Simeock nos chance with a rine drive, an4l made the scores equal. k'rom the centre-kick the game was a " ding-donger," with the visitors slightly the better. Millington was a great stumbling block to them, breaking up attacks without number. The home players cod not get past the visitors' half-back line, who now played a good defensive game. The Heath's inside forwards were most prominent with good combination. Smith placed the ball just over the home backs; Jones rushed up and Saville left his goal and just failed to reach the ball. Jones headed the ball into the empty goal and put the visitors ahead. As the end was approach- ing the home players seemed to give up their chance of recovering the lead, and the visitors easily held them in check. When the whistle blew the " Heathens " were deserving winners by two goals against one. The -" Heathens" played a good game all round, whilst Saville. Millington and Harrison showed up best for the Amateurs.

div.head: ADULT SCHOOLS.
div.p: THE ADULT SCHOOLS.
Decent Houses for Working - Class People : Demanded.
INTERESTING MEETINGS.

At Academy-street Men's School on Sunday Councillor Dr. McKee gave an instructive lee- tu.rette on "Diseases." He showed how these were directly or indirectly caused through heredity, climatic conditions, food, water supply, personal cleanliness and habits. He emphasised the need for influencing public Opinion in favour* of providing and ensuring not only pure food, milk, and water, but in the prevention of overcrowding, and its result- ant evils. *

Academy-street Women's. On Wednesday evening Mrs. J. A. Ransome took the Bible lesson on the `&1-lome as the cradle of the State." A subject '4ike this gave the speaker every opportunity of exercising her well-known method of drawing out the opinions of those present and summarising them into a unity.
Bew sey Men's.

Frank Worrall gave an interesting paper on " Food Prices" on Sunday morning. The essayist dealt with the rapid rise in prices and traced some of the causes. He specially em- phasised the effect which higher wages to the worker have had upon food supplies in sending up prices far and above legitimate levels, and Pointed out that the workers were getting worse off in consequence. Therefore advances in wages, without other and more remedial mea- sures, had disastrous effects 'on the purchasing power of wages.
Stockton Heath Men's.

This school had a visit on Sunday morning from Mr. Charles Madeley, who gave a most interesting lecture on "Transport and Travel in the reign of George III." Comparing the two periods, the time of George 111., say, 1760 to 1830, and the Victorian era, 1830-1900, which succeeded it, it may be claimed that in many departments of material activity greater pro- gress and more vital changes took place in the earlier than in the later' period. TO progress of the Victorian era consisted largely in the mere development of the inventions and im- provements introduced in the Georgian time. Incidentally, it happens that several of these important movements were inaugurated in or near 'Warrington, the Sankey Canal being the first, and the Bridgewater Canal the second English works of the kind.
Sankey Bridges Men's.

The second lecture on "The History of Trade Unionism" was postponed, owing to the un- avoidable absence of the lecturer. The Bibb lesson for the day was based on the childhood of Sesus, the subject being The School as a preparation for life." Mr. Barnard. in intro- ducing, said the home life and school life must go together, as without the help of the parents, the teacher is handicapped.

div.head: GREAT SANKEY.
div.p: GREAT SANKEY.

Lasted a Lifetime.—When the Clerk asked at the Parish Council meeting on Monday if there was anything in regard to the nuisance at the brook, Councillor Fair said he thought. it had gone on a lifetime, and he thought it would go on anther.

Guiding Motorists—Motorists passing through the village are going to be prevented from going astray on account of the obscure position of the Liverpool and Manchester main road finger- post. At the Parish Council meeting on Mon- day, the Clerk said the County Surveyor had given instructions to have the grievance reme- died.

Gas Reduction.—Recently the Parish Council applied for concessions in regard to the reduc- tion of gas, and on Monday the Parish Council were informed that the matter would come before the Warrington Gas Committee at their next meeting. It would appear that there will be a reduction if the Council take more lamps. and we understand this is what it is intended to do.

New Canal Bridge.—At the Parish Council meeting on Monday the Clerk read a letter from Mr. W. Compton Hall, Bridgemaster's Depart- ment, County Offices, Preston, in regard to the canal bridge. Mr. Hall said that the negotia- tions with the railway company had been very prolonged, and it was thought not desirable to disturb the existing bridge before the King's visit. They had now received authority from the Main Roads and Bridges Committee to obtain tenders. The work will probably be in hand in the near future.

A Dangerous Eiridge.Buttermilk Bridge is in a very dangerous state. At the Parish Council meeting on Monday Councillor Fair said some- one would be killed there if steps were not taken at once. The Clerk explained that the Warring- ton borough repaired one-half of the bridge, whereupon Councillor Fair said that the Parish Council staved their end, but the town end could be shaken loose It was decided to call the attention of the Warrington Corporation and the District Council to the unsafe state of the bridge. ti

A Water Question.—At the Parish Council meeting the Clerk explained that the Rural District Council had forwarded for the consid- eration of the Parish Council a request sent by certain residents in Hood-lane for the extension of the water main from the Rose Inn to the Cheshire Lines Railway Bridge, the cost being £22 for 20 years, less amount paid ,as water rates by the section. The Rural District Coun- cil also desired the advice of the Parish Council as to extending the water main from Brow Farm in Barrow Ha to Baguley's Farm, the cost being A;2O for 20 years.—After considerable discussion, which the Press were requested not to report, Councillor Pownall moved and Coun- cillor Ireland seconded, ," That the Council could not 'see their way at present to involve the parish in the expenditure of £22, unless there were some Prospects of some greater return being made by other properties being built or a pros- pect of them being built.—This resolution was carried.—ln regard to the other matter, Coun- cillor Furness (chairman)" asked if it was de- sirous to involve the parish in that expendi- ture on account of the farms.—Councillor Pow- nail: I don't think so.—The Clerk: I have no ' request in this case. They might all refuse to have the water, and then where shall we be. A penny rate would produce about .C32.—Council- lor Furness: I will •do all I can with the Dis- trict Council to induce the Warrington Corpora- tion to ,carry the mains as far as they possibly can without involving us into an annual charge or obligation.—The Clerk: I don't know who is interesting themselves in this, or where the sug- gestion emanates from.—The, foregoing resolu- tion was applied to this matter also.
A DEFECTIVE FOOTPATH. Who. is Responsible for Repairs?

The members who attended at the Parish Council meeting .on Monday evening were Messrs. W. Furness (chairman), W: 11. Ireland, S. Fair, J. G. Pownall, and R. ,Long, with Mr. J. Smith (clerk). • The chief topic discussed was the had condition of the field path leading from Hood-lane to Buttermilk Bridge. The general feeling was that something should be done im- mediately to ensure a safe passage to pedes- trians. -

The Clerk read a letter from the District Council, in which Mr. Sutfon said that by reso- lution long in force the Council had not under- taken any cost Of repairing field footpaths, and it was considered the duty of the parish to deal with it on their own account. He might sug- gest, however, that it might be useful to &infer with Mr. Newcombe, the surveyor, as to action taken by him with respect to action that ought to he taken by the owners.

The Clerk,stiid it was not a question of repair- ing the footpath, but of acquiring.: and to widen out the entrance to the road. It used to be an old custom for farmers or occupiers of land to repair field footpaths. The District Council had authority to acquire the strip of land they would

Plans may be seen and copies of Specification and Quantities obtained at the Office of the Engineers, Messrs. Wright and Hamlyn, San- key-street Chambers, Warrington, on payment of a deposit of One Guinea. which will be re- turned on receipt of a bona-fide tender. Sealed tenders, endorsed "Walton Inferior Sewerage," to be delivered to the undersigned not later than Twelve o'clock noon on Monday, the 3rd day of November. 1913. RUNCORN UNION. The Guardians of the above Union are prepared to receive TENDERS for Sundry Minor Alterations and Additional Fittings at the Workhouse Hospital, Dutton, according to Specification prepared by their Architects. Persons desirous of tendering may obtain copy of the specification from Messrs. Wright and Hamlyn, Sankey-street Chambers, Warrington, on a deposit of 10s. 6d. being received, which will be returned on receipt of a bona-fide tender. Sealed tenders, endorsed "Tender for Altera- tions, &c., Dutton Workhouse," must reach my Office, 71. High-street. Runcorn, not later than 12 o'clock noon on Monday, the 3rd day of November, 1913. The Guardians do not bind themselves to accept the lowest or any tender. By order, , GEO. F. ASHTON. Clerk to the Guardians. Runcorn, 16th October, 1913.

PADGATE SENSATION. Mysterious Drowning Case Yesterday Morning. WELL-KNOWN FARMER'S END. An event which has cast a gloom over the Fearnhead district took place yesterday morn- ing, when the body of Mr. T. Ashley (43), a well- known farmel', of Cinnamon Farm, Fearnhead, was discovered by Mr. John Unsworth, Hough- ton Green, a farm hand, in a pond adjacent to Mr'. Ashley's h9use. The police report states that deceased arrived home about 6.30 the previous, night, and after attending to his duties retired to bed about, nine p.m. l'e,sterday morning he got up at five o'clock, when his mother saw him for the last time alive. , P.Ol. Butterworth was called and deceased \vas taken to the farm. DAIRY INSTITUTE FOR CHESHIRE. The Agricultural Committee of the Cheshire County Council decided on Monday to recom- mend Ridley Hall and 170 acres of land ad- joining as suitable for the purposes of a Dairy Institute for Cheshire, and a deputation was appointed to wait upon the Board of Agricul- ture. Ridley Hall Estate was purchased some ' time ago by the Cheshire County. Council from Earl Cottenham for -t50,000 /for use as small holdings. MOORE. Wesley Guild.—On Wednesday evening Mr. Moss, of Lymm, favoured the Guild with an- other of his very interesting lectures, entitled "Livingstone in Africa," which Was illustrated by many beautiful and interesting slides. Mr. Moss, jun., ably manipulated the lantern. A very good attendance was presided over by Mr. Thomas Plumpton.
